name: Wednesday
label: Dead Oceans
lede: Karly Hartzman started Wednesday as a solo project while still a photography student in Asheville, and named it after a British jangle-pop band. Eight years on, the five-piece with the pedal steel and the feedback has Pitchfork's No. 6 album of 2025.

eras.title: A Bandcamp page and a borrowed name
eras.text: Hartzman records yep definitely with a college friend, sings in a pop-punk band on the side, and lets a guitarist named MJ Lenderman sleep over after a show. By the end of 2018 he's on a Wednesday EP.

years.big: I learned how to play guitar watching Tiny Desk concerts.
years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: Karly Hartzman · NPR Tiny Desk: Wednesday · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: [[Karly Hartzman|92ec14cd-1631-4724-98e8-b28da18360a8]] names her solo project after the Sundays
years.p: Hartzman, then a photography student at UNC Asheville, on how she picked up the instrument. The name comes from the British band [[The Sundays|9df32318-47d5-4df7-bc68-3ed9e15eb0f6]].
years.xp:
Hartzman wanted to combine the Sundays' vocals with the guitar noise of [[Swirlies|4ec4a033-ba44-41ca-8e09-3bf94fc08523]] and country writing, according to Wikipedia. In her own 2024 Tiny Desk introduction she credited the NPR series, and especially [[Mitski|fa58cf24-0e44-421d-8519-8bf461dcfaa5]]'s 2015 set, as her guitar school.

She grew up in Greensboro, North Carolina, and told Stereogum she'd picked up a ukulele in middle school.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: Karly Hartzman
years.h: [[MJ Lenderman|4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc]] sleeps over at the Hartzmans' after a show
years.p: That's how the two Asheville songwriters meet, at her family's house. They'll be together for six years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: yep definitely comes out of a campus studio
years.p: Hartzman and [[Daniel Gorham|e8f169df-d199-4262-b48a-cd42b9382423]], a college friend, make it as a duo, and it goes up on Bandcamp before there's a band to play it.
years.xp: It came out January 31, 2018, self-released. Paste and Stereogum both call it a solo debut, recorded at a campus studio and blending dream-pop and indie rock.

years.src: Wikipedia: Karly Hartzman · Stereogum: Band To Watch
years.h: Hartzman picks up a second band, Diva Sweetly
years.p: The pop-punk band is a Pictures of Vernon spin-off, and she plays on its 2019 album In The Living Room while Wednesday grows on the side.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: MJ Lenderman
years.h: How Do You Let Love Into the Heart That Isn't Split Wide Open
years.p: This December 2018 EP on Sub-Fi is, per Wikipedia, the first Wednesday release with Lenderman on it.

eras.title: Five people, one lap steel
eras.text: Hartzman hires from the scenes she already works in: a drummer from local shows, a steel player from the Mothlight, a bassist, and the guitarist she's dating. The records get louder, and a small Asheville label, Orindal, puts them out.

years.src: Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Mountain Xpress: Wednesday primes · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: Asheville does the hiring: [[Alan Miller|3dfb54e2-83c8-4e99-b44b-5fafb6dc0eae]] and [[Xandy Chelmis|cc52f05a-4006-44a8-8d0d-1ce50fe4942e]]
years.p: Paste says Hartzman met Miller at local shows and Chelmis while both worked at the Mothlight, the West Asheville venue that closed after nearly a decade.
years.xp:
Mountain Xpress reports she also interned at the Mothlight and got early opening slots there. Opening for Speedy Ortiz in 2019 was, she said, a "we were losing our minds" night. Paste adds that she and Chelmis went to metal shows there together.

The sources don't agree on years: Wikipedia has Miller from 2017 and Chelmis from 2020, and the stints on this page follow Wikipedia.

years.src: Mountain Xpress: Wednesday primes · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: Wednesday's first full-band record comes out on Orindal Records
years.p: I Was Trying to Describe You to Someone was made in a bedroom studio. Gorham leaves around the same time for Prince Daddy & the Hyena.
years.xp:
Mountain Xpress calls it a bedroom-studio job. Paste has Gorham leaving after the record, while Wikipedia gives his stint as 2017 to 2019. Miller told Paste that with Gorham the band had "very different styles at play".

Twelve days after release, the band recorded a live session of November at DZ Records.

years.src: Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Wikipedia: Twin Plagues
years.h: Wednesday becomes a five-piece, with [[Margo Schultz|66fd0ab1-1756-4dcf-9f39-5a0f626947f9]] on bass and Lenderman on lead
years.p: Paste says Hartzman was a fan of his solo songs while working in food service before he became a full member around Twin Plagues.

years.src: Wikipedia: Twin Plagues · WUNC: The world according to Wednesday · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat
years.h: Pitchfork gives Twin Plagues a 7.4
years.p: The first record of the Lenderman era, recorded at Drop of Sun with Alex Farrar and Adam McDaniel, lands at No. 31 on Paste's 2021 list.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Kelly Liu described the sound as big and loud with an undercurrent of anxiety. Paste calls it the band's breakthrough, a mix of hardcore, shoegaze, post-punk and folk rock.

The album introduces Gary, a bar-fight character Hartzman brings back on Bleeds as "Gary's II". It also has a cover of Edie Brickell's "Ghost of a Dog".

years.src: WUNC: Why Asheville's Drop of Sun
years.h: Drop of Sun, the studio two UNC Asheville grads built on Haywood Road
years.p: Adam McDaniel and Alex Farrar started it in 2015. It becomes the room where Wednesday, Lenderman, Indigo De Souza and Angel Olsen record.

eras.title: A scream and a signature
eras.text: A covers album pays back the bands Wednesday learned from. Then an 8.5-minute single ends in a scream, and Dead Oceans signs the band.

years.src: Stereogum: Hear Wednesday Cover
years.h: Smashing Pumpkins and Gary Stewart share a covers album
years.p: Wednesday plays songs by [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]], [[Medicine|0f24bcb0-8d37-409d-aed1-92bd4e5337ed]], [[Chris Bell|db6ac2f7-5bbb-4ed4-88f4-540d5b29542a]], [[Drive-By Truckers|8eae1e0a-1696-4532-9e3c-0a072217ef4c]], Roger Miller and others, recorded in Durham with Alli Rogers.
years.xp: Stereogum reports it was released on Orindal and includes three covers first recorded for Aquarium Drunkard in January 2022. Hartzman said the band wanted to repay in part the "huge debt" it owed those artists, and that the songs share sadness with humor.

years.cap: Wednesday at Rose Bowl Tavern, the opening night of their tour
years.src: Wikipedia: Bull Believer · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Wikipedia: Rat Saw God
years.h: Dead Oceans signs Wednesday on the last day of tracking
years.p: The first single from the album, Bull Believer, runs 8.5 minutes and ends with Hartzman screaming.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the lyrics started from a George Jones episode of the podcast Cocaine & Rhinestones that included Spanish bullfighting history. Hartzman was self-conscious about screaming, so she recorded that section alone while the band played Tetris elsewhere in the studio. She said it was maybe the third time she had ever screamed.

Lenderman told Paste: "When I see it coming up on setlist, my fingers start bleeding." Pitchfork later ranked it No. 92 of 2022's songs and Paste ranked it fifth.

eras.title: Year of the Rat
eras.text: Rat Saw God takes Wednesday out of the Southeast. A year of touring leaves a new bassist on stage, and an anti-Amazon speech on Amazon's.

years.cap: Wednesday on stage in Grand Rapids, Michigan, September 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: Rat Saw God · Nylon: Rock Band Wednesday · Paste: Wednesday's Year of the Rat · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: Rat Saw God takes Pitchfork's No. 4 spot of 2023
years.p: Pitchfork gave it an 8.8. Recorded at Drop of Sun with Farrar, it is first on both Paste's and Stereogum's year-end lists.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Sam Sodomsky gave it the 8.8, and Metacritic assigned 89, per Wikipedia. Nylon reported that Pitchfork named it Best New Music. Paste says the title is borrowed from an episode of Veronica Mars.

Chelmis told Paste the Drop of Sun crew were "really sweet people who just wanted to hook us up with a good recording experience." It is the last Wednesday album with Schultz, who also painted the six-foot oil painting on the cover.

years.src: Nylon: Rock Band Wednesday · Mountain Xpress: Wednesday primes · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: [[Ethan Baechtold|6eaef41e-66a3-467c-a437-58b028b88058]] takes the bass from Schultz before the spring tours
years.p: He plays the spring 2023 U.S. tour and the first European tour.

years.cap: Hartzman playing guitar in Grand Rapids, Michigan, September 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: Bull Believer
years.h: Hartzman speaks against Amazon from Amazon Music's stage
years.p: At Primavera Sound in Barcelona she dedicates Bull Believer to warehouse workers who have been mistreated.
years.xp: Wikipedia and its Bull Believer article place the speech on the Amazon Music stage at Primavera Sound, on June 4, 2023.

eras.title: The room gets bigger, the band changes shape
eras.text: Wednesday plays the Tiny Desk in March. The same month, Hartzman and Lenderman split up on tour in Japan, and the news stays out of the public for a while. In September, Hurricane Helene hits Asheville.

years.cap: Hartzman singing and playing guitar with Wednesday in Pittsburgh, January 2024
years.src: NPR Tiny Desk: Wednesday
years.h: Hartzman plays the Tiny Desk she learned guitar from
years.p: Wednesday play Chosen to Deserve, Formula One and Bath County, with Chelmis on pedal steel, lap steel and banjo.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · Wikipedia: MJ Lenderman · Paste: Wednesday Rejoice
years.h: Hartzman and Lenderman break up in Tokyo after six years
years.p: They split while touring Japan, per Wikipedia, and keep it from the rest of the band at first. Most Bleeds songs are already written.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the breakup to March 2024 and says Lenderman revealed it in a July 2024 Guardian interview. Lenderman's page cites a February 2025 GQ interview.

Hartzman told Paste: "we care about each other, it wasn't difficult for me to accept that that's what he needed."

years.src: WUNC: Why Asheville's Drop of Sun
years.h: Hurricane Helene hits Asheville, and the scene organizes
years.p: Drop of Sun cofounder Adam McDaniel's nonprofit Lamplight AVL raised $145,000 in artist grants, and a benefit compilation followed in March 2025.

eras.title: A record made a month after the breakup
eras.text: Lenderman leaves the touring band and stays in the studio, Hartzman moves home to Greensboro, and Wednesday lands on Colbert, then on a Weezer single.

years.cap: Lenderman on guitar with Wednesday in Grand Rapids, Michigan
years.src: Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band) · JamBase: Wednesday Toast
years.h: Lenderman steps off the road and stays in the studio
years.p: He says he'll focus on his solo career. Hartzman calls him a non-negotiable part of the band's identity.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Lenderman said he would remain a full contributing member in the studio. Jake "Spyder" Pugh has since played lead guitar live.

years.src: Stereogum: Watch Wednesday Make · JamBase: Wednesday Toast
years.h: "Elderberry Wine" is Wednesday's TV debut, on Colbert
years.p: Lenderman joins the band on The Late Show, weeks after announcing he was leaving the road.
years.xp: Stereogum dates the performance to May 22 and JamBase to May 21. Both note it was the band's first new music since Rat Saw God. Hartzman described the song as being about how the sweet things in life can turn to poison if they aren't tended.

years.cap: Wednesday at Circolo Arci Bellezza, Milan
years.src: Wikipedia: Bleeds · BRICKS Magazine · Clash: The Way Love Goes · Album of the Year · Paste: Wednesday Rejoice
years.h: Bleeds is recorded a month after the split
years.p: Recorded again at Drop of Sun with Alex Farrar. Pitchfork gives it 8.7, then ranks it No. 6 of 2025.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Pitchfork 8.7, Metacritic 88, PopMatters 9 and Uncut 9. BRICKS quotes The Guardian calling it the year's best alt-rock album. Hartzman described it as the spiritual successor to Rat Saw God and the "quintessential Wednesday Creek Rock album". The working title, rejected, was Carolina Girl.

Singles were "Elderberry Wine", "Wound Up Here (By Holdin On)", "Pick Up That Knife" and "Bitter Everyday". Hartzman said many songs were written while she and Lenderman were together, and recorded a month after they split.

years.src: Paste: Wednesday Rejoice · WUNC: The world according to Wednesday
years.h: "Gary's II" closes the album with a bar fight and a landlord
years.p: The song honors the late Gary King, Hartzman's Haw Creek landlord. She wanted to preserve his stories before they were lost.
years.xp: Paste says it follows "Gary's" from Twin Plagues and mentions a bar fight and Gary's false teeth.

years.big: If Xandy was not in this band, Wednesday is over.
years.src: Paste: Wednesday Rejoice
years.h: The member Hartzman says the band can't lose
years.p: Karly Hartzman to Paste about Chelmis, who she met working at the Mothlight. He plays pedal steel, lap steel and banjo, and sings backing vocals.

years.src: Wikipedia: We Might as Well · Wikipedia: Wednesday (American band)
years.h: Weezer's "We Might as Well Be Strangers" features Hartzman and Chelmis
years.p: They share the song from Weezer's twentieth album, the first Weezer collaboration since 2014.
